items.title: David Friesen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2024
items.q: It seemed to me that you had something pretty innovative there, almost like Stanley Jordan when he did his guitar thing.

ctx.x: Yeah. I just called it a map. I didn’t want to confuse you. Sorry.

That’s okay. I wanted to see if I could compare a couple of your compositions. If we go way back to 1976 and you recorded the “Duet and Dialogue” I think the entry that I had that I was going to read from the Grove, it had this sentence, “His experimentation with techniques may be heard on “Duet and Dialogue” where he plays with the bow and plucks the strings with both hands.” It seemed to me that you had something pretty innovative there, almost like Stanley Jordan when he did his guitar thing. If you compare…

Well I’m sure it has. I don’t think about things like that if I’m understanding your question clearly. I really don’t think about things like that. It’s important for me to stay in the moment and so I won’t spend time — yeah, I don’t know if I’m answering your question correctly. I don’t consider that or think about that or plan for that. I just —when it’s time to feed the dogs I feed the dogs. When it’s time — I just don’t spend time — my time musically is spent — I’ve been playing a lot of piano lately and…
